title: Rafael and the Salt
premise: Yara Eriksen, a royal food-taster who has spent years dosing herself with poison to survive the king's table, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Salt Guild—a shadowy brotherhood that trades in impossible things: bottled grief, borrowed names, years of life. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Yara learns the child is a key: the king has been unbound from his own body, and the thing wearing his crown feeds on the realm's memory. To save him, Yara must break her guild's oldest law—revealing the ledgers—and choose between the loyalty that made her and the truth that could unmake everything. In the end she dissolves the Salt Guild itself, trading her own recorded name to free the king, and walks away remembered by no one except the child, who alone can speak her true name back into the world.
about_author: August Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from drowned port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose quiet jobs sit too close to power.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She survives another poisoned dish at court while memorizing which noble wants which rival dead. Introduces her double life: taster by day, ledger-keeper for the Salt Guild by night. Emotional beat: controlled numbness masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Yara catalogs the guild's inventory—bottled grief, a stolen decade, someone's first love—in the cellar archive. Her handler, Corvane, warns her never to read past her own entries. Beat: curiosity as quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: A mud-soaked girl appears at Yara's lodging speaking no known tongue, clutching a salt-white coin stamped with the guild's mark. The girl's words make Yara's old scars ache. Beat: fear and inexplicable recognition.

chapters.title: What the King Ate
chapters.summary: At court, Yara notices the king no longer tastes anything—food passes his lips like ash. His eyes are wrong in small ways. She begins logging his symptoms beside her poison records. Beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Corvane's Warning
chapters.summary: The guild summons Yara; Corvane orders the child surrendered to the guild 'for processing.' Yara lies for the first time in her career, hiding the girl in the archive. Beat: loyalty cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Yara finds the child's speech matches marginalia in the guild's oldest ledger—a pre-kingdom script called the Root-Tongue. The girl draws the king's crown with a serpent beneath it. Beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Through a guild scrying-glass, Yara sees the truth: something ancient wears the king, and it has been slowly eating the realm's memories—roads vanish, names fade from documents. Beat: vertigo of realizing the world is being edited.

chapters.title: Entries That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Auditing the ledgers, Yara discovers pages about herself she never wrote—including an entry dated three days from now describing her death. Beat: terror and fatalism.

chapters.title: Salt and Debt
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how orphaned Yara was recruited—the guild bought her debts, gave her immunity training, and claimed her name as collateral. Beat: understanding that her invisibility was always a cage.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers
chapters.summary: The child, whom Yara names Vess, begins remembering fragments aloud; each word restores a lost street or song to the city around them. Beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Yara returns to the palace; the queen's memory of her wedding day is gone, replaced by blank devotion. The crowned thing tests Yara with a dish she cannot identify. Beat: performance under mortal scrutiny.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Clause
chapters.summary: Corvane reveals the guild's founding bargain: centuries ago they bound the ancient thing beneath the crown in exchange for their trade. The guild didn't imprison it—they feed it. Beat: betrayal of every belief Yara held.

chapters.title: Running the Archive
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers search for Vess. Yara uses her mastery of the ledgers' cross-references to hide the girl inside a false entry, erasing her from guild sight. Beat: competence as defiance.

chapters.title: An Ally With Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Yara recruits Tam, a young palace scribe who noticed the memory-loss discrepancies, risking his career and life. Their alliance sparks something warmer. Beat: trust as vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: Yara's decades of poison-dosing begin failing—her body is breaking down faster than her entries predicted. Time limit established: she has weeks. Beat: mortality made urgent.

chapters.title: What Vess Is
chapters.summary: Deciphering the Root-Tongue, Yara learns Vess is not a child but a vessel: the last living fragment of the king's original soul, cast out when the thing took him. Beat: compassion deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Guild Conclave
chapters.summary: Masked masters convene; Yara attends as ledger-keeper and witnesses them vote to deliver Vess to the crowned thing to renew their bargain. Beat: isolation among her own people.

chapters.title: Stolen Pages
chapters.summary: Tam forges a writ while Yara copies the binding ritual from the sealed First Ledger. Corvane catches them—but instead of reporting, he looks away, haunted by his own history. Beat: unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: The Queen's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: The queen privately begs Yara to find what happened to her husband, revealing she suspects but cannot hold the thought long enough to act. Beat: grief without memory, love without object.

chapters.title: Root-Tongue Lessons
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Vess teaches Yara the old language in the archive; each learned word costs Yara a memory of her childhood. Love against sacrifice crystallizes. Beat: tenderness amid loss.

chapters.title: The Bargain Renewed
chapters.summary: The guild delivers a decoy child to the palace; the crowned thing accepts it, and the city loses an entire season overnight—harvests, funerals, births, all unwritten. Beat: horror at scale.

chapters.title: Yara's Death, As Recorded
chapters.summary: The prophesied entry comes due: enforcers ambush Yara at the drop-house. She survives only because the entry named the wrong hour—someone altered her ledger. Beat: paranoia and gratitude.

chapters.title: Who Rewrote Me
chapters.summary: Investigation reveals Corvane edited her death-entry, spending thirty years of his own recorded life to buy her an escape. He confesses she reminds him of the person he was before the guild. Beat: loyalty redefined as love of truth.

chapters.title: Into the Under-Court
chapters.summary: Following Vess's memories, the trio descends through the palace foundations to the original throne room where the binding was struck. Beat: descent into the story's buried heart.

chapters.title: The First Ledger's Truth
chapters.summary: In the under-court, the First Ledger reveals the full bargain: the guild's founders were the thing's first victims, and every trade since has fed it memory. The guild is its digestive system. Beat: total collapse of Yara's worldview.

chapters.title: The Crowned Thing Speaks
chapters.summary: The entity addresses Yara directly through the king's mouth, offering her anything—her name back, her health, Tam safe—if she surrenders Vess. Beat: temptation aimed precisely at her wounds.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Yara refuses, and the thing takes the offer off the table: it will take the city's remaining memory in nine days unless Vess is delivered. Countdown begins. Beat: resolve hardened by threat.

chapters.title: Rallying the Tasters
chapters.summary: Yara recruits the other food-tasters—all guild-collateralized orphans like her—using their shared immunity training as a network to move unseen. Beat: solidarity of the invisible.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam is offered a royal appointment that would erase his debts and his connection to Yara. He burns the appointment letter. Beat: love choosing duty to a person over duty to a system.

chapters.title: Unbinding, Part One: The Words
chapters.summary: Vess completes the Root-Tongue instruction; Yara learns the unbinding requires a name freely given by someone the king's true self trusted. No one living qualifies—except, impossibly, an entry in Yara's own ledger. Beat: hope with a terrible shape.

chapters.title: The Entry in My Hand
chapters.summary: Yara discovers the king, years ago, anonymously saved a starving orphan girl and recorded her debt in the guild book—that girl was Yara. He trusted her before she ever knew him. Beat: destiny reframed as kindness repaid.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: Corvane openly defects, giving Yara the conclave's seal; the masters send enforcers to seize Vess early. A running battle through the archive destroys centuries of ledgers. Beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: Burning the Books
chapters.summary: Yara realizes the ledgers themselves anchor the thing's feeding. She sets the archive alight, freeing thousands of traded lives but erasing her own recorded name forever. Beat: sacrifice as identity crisis.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Spent
chapters.summary: With the countdown nearly expired, the weakened thing begins consuming the capital wholesale; landmarks gray out, citizens forget their children mid-embrace. Beat: apocalyptic urgency.

chapters.title: The Throne Room
chapters.summary: Yara, Vess, Tam, and Corvane fight through the collapsing palace to the under-court throne. The crowned thing, starving, wears the king's face and pleads in his voice. Beat: climax threshold, mercy versus necessity.

chapters.title: Unbinding, Part Two: The Name Given
chapters.summary: Yara speaks the king's true name—which she alone now carries, via the debt-entry—and offers her own in exchange. Vess pours the king's soul-fragment home. The thing unravels, screaming in every forgotten language. Beat: climax, love defeating hunger.

chapters.title: The King Waking
chapters.summary: The real king wakes with no memory of the lost years; the queen remembers him all at once and weeps. He seeks the stranger who freed him, but Yara is already gone—unrecorded, unnamed. Beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the guild dissolves, its survivors scattering; Corvane, aged decades by his spent years, becomes the keeper of a single honest record. Tam chooses to stay near Yara even though he barely recalls why. Beat: quiet reconstruction.

chapters.title: The Name Spoken Back
chapters.summary: Vess, the only being who ever knew Yara outside the ledgers, speaks her true name aloud in Root-Tongue, restoring her to herself—not as the guild's property, but as her own. Beat: identity reclaimed through love.

chapters.title: Rafael and the Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Yara's POV. Revealed: Rafael was the name the king wrote in the ledger for the orphan girl he saved—the name Yara was always meant to have. She and Tam open a plain kitchen where nothing is traded and everything is tasted honestly. Beat: peace earned, identity chosen.
